items.query: How is interest compounded on an FX3-C mortgage?
items.answer_text:
Fixed-rate interest on FX3-C is compounded semi-annually. [S1][S3]

Mortgage Operations converts the stated annual rate to a payment-period rate using i = (1 + r / 2)^(2 / f) - 1, where r is the annual rate as a decimal and f is the number of payments per year. [S3]

Each FX3-C payment is calculated under this method and rounded to the cent. [S2]

What rate is used to qualify a borrower for VR5-C?
items.answer_text:
The qualifying rate for VR5-C is the greater of the contract rate plus 1.75 points or 5.40% [S1].
Using the rate sheet effective 2026-11-01, the calculation is as follows [S1].
- Step 1: DMC Prime of 4.70% minus 0.55 points gives a contract rate of 4.15% [S1].
- Step 2: The contract rate of 4.15% plus 1.75 points gives 5.90% [S1].
- Step 3: Because 5.90% is more than the 5.40% floor, the qualifying rate is 5.90% [S1].
The qualifying rate is a testing rate and is not the rate the borrower pays [S1].
Every VR5-C application is tested at the qualifying rate under POL-004 [S4][S5].

- Step 3: The 5.40% floor is lower than 5.90%, so the qualifying rate is 5.90%. [S1]

items.query: When a client puts less than 20% down, what extra cover must be arranged?
items.answer_text:
When the down payment is less than 20% of the purchase price, the mortgage needs mortgage default insurance [S2].
A down payment below 20% leads to a loan-to-value ratio above 80%, so the borrower needs this insurance [S3].
The insurance must be arranged with an approved mortgage default insurer, and it must be in place before Demo Mortgage Co. funds the loan [S3].
Underwriting must confirm that the insurer has approved the loan before the file is approved [S3].
